purpose: P2 disposition ledger (T-O-11). harden = apply a low-cost fence/validation that does not change the feature contract; accept = record as accepted local self-impact because a fix would change the feature (per T-O-3 a contract-changing fix must not ship). optionalHardening/monitoring/ownerSignoff/reviewDate are filled in Phase 4.

risks.subject: dsh-nano-explorer-extra /create-file /create-folder /rename /move /delete
risks.existingFeature: Workspace file mutations follow symlinks as ordinary entries; a link pointing outside the workspace is currently followed.
risks.rationale: Realpath fence at the last trusted decision point so mutations cannot escape the workspace root via symlink. Registered as 'harden + edge behaviour change' per T-O-14-3: links pointing outside the workspace will start being refused.

risks.subject: dsh-nano-explorer-extra /commit /pull /checkout
risks.existingFeature: Git add/commit/checkout runs `git` as the host user; an attacker-planted .git/config filter driver or smudge/clean filter executes during these ops.
risks.rationale: Refuse to run git write ops against a worktree whose .git/** content can be planted by page routes (deny .git mutation / scrub filter config) without removing the SCM UI.

risks.subject: dsh-nano-model-selector /imagine (grok engine template)
risks.existingFeature: The grok template copies live ~/.grok/{auth.json,config.toml} into workspace imagine/.grok so the CLI can run sandboxed.
risks.rationale: Stop copying live credentials into the workspace: write a .gitignore for imagine/.grok and/or add a SKIP path so the real token is not planted in a synced/commit-able directory.

risks.subject: dsh-nano-explorer-extra scopeOf() (all session routes)
risks.existingFeature: scopeOf resolves ANY existing sessionId, letting a page script adopt another session's workspace and weakest sandboxPolicy.
risks.rationale: Add observability/limited binding (log + warn on foreign sessionId) — only logging, since the explorer intentionally lets the page pick any session and tightening could break multi-session use.

risks.subject: dsh-nano-explorer-extra /read /list
risks.existingFeature: /read returns any UTF-8 host file (≤1MiB) when client sends allowOutsideWorkspace:true; /list enumerates arbitrary host directories.
risks.rationale: Removing outside-workspace reads would break documented preview/open behaviours (same-user page self-impact, P2). requestRejection is the gate; accept and note optional fence.

risks.subject: dsh-nano-notepad /read
risks.existingFeature: /read returns any host UTF-8 text file (≤2MiB, previously *.md/*.markdown) without workspace confinement.
risks.rationale: Arbitrary-text-file open is the feature (open any note path). Confining it would remove the open-anywhere workflow; same-user self-impact, accept.

risks.subject: dsh-nano-shared-workspace /ls /mkdir
risks.existingFeature: /ls and /mkdir accept arbitrary absolute paths so the join/create dialog can browse and create a replica dir anywhere.
risks.rationale: Free directory browsing/mkdir is the documented join workflow; fencing to the workspace would remove it. Same-user self-impact, accept.

risks.subject: dsh-nano-notepad /s3/config
risks.existingFeature: Settings UI lets the user set any S3-compatible endpoint; the host signs probes with stored credentials, making a signed-SSRF oracle.
risks.rationale: Multi-endpoint cloud sync is the feature; restricting endpoints would change it. Same-user config of own storage, accept (cross-tenant write abuse is covered by the P0 schema work, not this route).

risks.subject: dsh-nano-explorer-extra /perf-review/host?mode=window
risks.existingFeature: mode=window drains and returns the process-global perf window (cross-plugin/session samples) for lab use.
risks.rationale: Window drain is the intended lab observability behaviour and only active when DSH_PERF_REVIEW=1; low severity, accept.
